title: Plougonvelin Stirling Memorial
memorial_details: Memorial stone and plaque in the grounds of private property, Plougonvelin, Finistère.
narrative: Stirling EF188 of 149 Squadron, coded OJ-M, departed Methwold at 2314 on 23 June 1944 on a gardening (minelaying) operation. The aircraft is believed to have been hit by Flak. Two crew baled out into the sea and drowned. The aircraft crashed into a farmhouse at approximately 0200 on 24 June. All seven crew were killed. Four civilians were also killed; a fifth died of injuries on 25 June 1944.
cause_of_loss: Believed hit by Flak; crashed into a farmhouse
community_connection: The aircraft crashed into a farmhouse near Plougonvelin. Four civilians were killed immediately; a fifth died of injuries the following day.

sources.title: Chorley, W.R. — Bomber Command Losses Vol. 5
